Standardizing plant names with WorldFloraFast

Source: vignettes/WorldFloraFast.Rmd
WorldFloraFast.Rmd

WorldFloraFast matches plant names against the taxonomic backbone of the World Flora Online (WFO): it corrects spelling mistakes, recognises synonyms and returns the currently accepted names. It is a faster, refactored derivative of the WorldFlora package (Kindt 2020), with the same functions and arguments.

1. Obtain the backbone

The backbone (classification.csv, about 1.6 million names) is published on Zenodo. WFO.download() downloads the latest release, verifies its checksum, remembers where it is and loads it as WFO.data:

WFO.download(save.dir = "wfo_data")              # first time: about 1 GB
WFO.download(save.dir = "wfo_data", update = TRUE)  # later: newer release?
# new session: load WFO.data again
WFO.remember()
WFO.data <- WFO.read("wfo_data", core.only = TRUE)  # or read fewer columns

This vignette uses WFO.example2026, a small extract of the WFO Plant List 2026-06 that is included in the package.

data(WFO.example2026)
head(WFO.example2026[, c(
  "taxonID", "scientificName", "taxonRank", "taxonomicStatus"
)])
#>          taxonID scientificName taxonRank taxonomicStatus
#> 1 wfo-4100000110         Palmae    family         Synonym
#> 2 wfo-1200070526    Reinwardtia     genus         Synonym
#> 3 wfo-4000034168       Saurauia     genus        Accepted
#> 4 wfo-7000000046      Arecaceae    family        Accepted
#> 5 wfo-4000027807          Palma     genus         Synonym
#> 6 wfo-4000029298        Phoenix     genus        Accepted

2. Prepare names that include authors

Names in field data or literature often include authors. WFO.prepare() separates them; the Authorship column then helps to choose between homonyms.

x <- c(
  "Faidherbia albida (Delile) A.Chev.", "Acacia albida Delile",
  "Pygeum afric Hook. f."
)
prep <- WFO.prepare(x, verbose = FALSE)
prep[, c("spec.full", "spec.name", "Authorship")]
#>                            spec.full         spec.name       Authorship
#> 1 Faidherbia albida (Delile) A.Chev. Faidherbia albida (Delile) A.Chev.
#> 2               Acacia albida Delile     Acacia albida           Delile
#> 3              Pygeum afric Hook. f.      Pygeum afric         Hook. f.

3. Match the names 

m <- WFO.match(prep, WFO.data = WFO.example2026, verbose = FALSE)
m[, c(
  "spec.name", "Subseq", "Fuzzy", "scientificName",
  "scientificNameAuthorship", "Old.name", "Old.author"
)]
#>           spec.name Subseq Fuzzy     scientificName scientificNameAuthorship
#> 1 Faidherbia albida      1 FALSE  Faidherbia albida         (Delile) A.Chev.
#> 2     Acacia albida      1 FALSE  Faidherbia albida         (Delile) A.Chev.
#> 3     Acacia albida      2 FALSE Vachellia tortuosa   (L.) Seigler & Ebinger
#> 4     Acacia albida      3 FALSE      Acacia albida             Rojas Acosta
#> 5      Pygeum afric      1  TRUE    Prunus africana        (Hook.f.) Kalkman
#>           Old.name Old.author
#> 1                            
#> 2    Acacia albida     Delile
#> 3    Acacia albida     Lindl.
#> 4                            
#> 5 Pygeum africanum    Hook.f.
  • Faidherbia albida is matched exactly.
  • Acacia albida has three homonyms in the WFO: A. albida Delile is a synonym of Faidherbia albida, A. albida Lindl. a synonym of Vachellia tortuosa, and A. albida Rojas Acosta is an accepted name. All three are returned, numbered by Subseq; synonyms are replaced by their accepted names and kept in Old.name.
  • Pygeum afric is incomplete: fuzzy matching finds Pygeum africanum, a synonym of Prunus africana.

Names can also be given as a character vector, or in separate columns Genus, Species, Infraspecific.rank and Infraspecific (exact matching only).

4. Keep one match per name

WFO.one() keeps one row per submitted name. With the distances between submitted and matched authors, the homonym A. albida Delile is chosen:

one <- WFO.one(m,
  Auth.dist = "Auth.dist", Old.author.dist = "Old.author.dist",
  verbose = FALSE
)
one[, c("spec.name", "Authorship", "scientificName", "Old.name", "One.Reason")]
#>           spec.name       Authorship    scientificName         Old.name
#> 1 Faidherbia albida (Delile) A.Chev. Faidherbia albida                 
#> 2     Acacia albida           Delile Faidherbia albida    Acacia albida
#> 5      Pygeum afric         Hook. f.   Prunus africana Pygeum africanum
#>                          One.Reason
#> 1                                  
#> 2 Authorship best match for synonym
#> 5

Without authors, WFO.one() prefers accepted names, then names that were not synonyms (here A. albida Rojas Acosta), then the smallest taxonID; One.Reason shows what decided.

Fuzzy matching options

Fuzzy is the maximum distance (a fraction of the name length, or a number of edits). By default only the closest candidates are kept (Fuzzy.min = TRUE); with Fuzzy.min = FALSE, all candidates within the distance are returned, one row each:

all.cand <- WFO.match("Omalanthus populneus",
  WFO.data = WFO.example2026,
  Fuzzy.min = FALSE, verbose = FALSE
)
all.cand[, c(
  "Subseq", "Fuzzy.dist", "scientificName", "taxonomicStatus", "Old.name"
)]
#>   Subseq Fuzzy.dist         scientificName taxonomicStatus
#> 1      1          9 Homalanthus caloneurus        Accepted
#> 2      2          2  Homalanthus populneus        Accepted
#> 3      3          2  Homalanthus populneus       Unchecked
#> 4      4         19 Homalanthus caloneurus        Accepted
#> 5      5         16  Homalanthus populneus        Accepted
#> 6      6         14  Homalanthus populneus        Accepted
#> 7      7         13  Homalanthus populneus        Accepted
#> 8      8         14        Alchornea sicca        Accepted
#>                                 Old.name
#> 1                                       
#> 2                                       
#> 3                                       
#> 4 Homalanthus populneus var. cordifolius
#> 5    Homalanthus populneus var. genuinus
#> 6      Homalanthus populneus var. laevis
#> 7       Homalanthus populneus var. minor
#> 8      Homalanthus populneus var. siccus

Fuzzy.dist is the distance to the name that was matched, which for replaced synonyms is Old.name (here, varieties replaced by their species).

5. Names that need more than spelling corrections

By default, WFO.match() uses the matching steps of WorldFlora, with three corrections that can each be switched off: a correctly spelled genus is not replaced by another one (Fuzzy.keep.genus), fuzzy matches must have a similar epithet (Fuzzy.epithet.check), and placeholders such as “indet.” or “sp.” are not matched (Fuzzy.skip.placeholder). When neither a name nor its first two words are found, it falls back to the genus. WorldFloraFast offers three optional steps for such names, switched off by default:

  • genus, then epithet (Fuzzy.genus): for truncated or misspelled genera;
  • genus transfer (Fuzzy.transfer): the same epithet in another genus of the family, when the backbone shows that species moved from the submitted genus to that genus;
  • strict genus fall-back (Fuzzy.one.strict): the genus only when the first word is an accepted genus name, so that local names are not given a scientific name.
x <- c(
  "Reinwardtiod cinerum", "Chrysophyllum madagascariensis", "Palma colorada"
)
m0 <- WFO.match(x, WFO.data = WFO.example2026, verbose = FALSE)
default <- WFO.one(m0, verbose = FALSE)
edge <- WFO.match(x,
  WFO.data = WFO.example2026, verbose = FALSE,
  Fuzzy.genus = TRUE, Fuzzy.transfer = TRUE, Fuzzy.one.strict = TRUE
)
data.frame(
  submitted = x, default = default$scientificName,
  optional.steps = ifelse(edge$Matched, edge$scientificName, "(not matched)")
)
#>                        submitted       default              optional.steps
#> 1           Reinwardtiod cinerum   Reinwardtia Reinwardtiodendron cinereum
#> 2 Chrysophyllum madagascariensis Chrysophyllum          Gambeya boiviniana
#> 3                 Palma colorada       Phoenix               (not matched)
  • “Reinwardtiod cinerum” is Reinwardtiodendron cinereum: the epithet is found in the genus that starts with “Reinwardtiod” (and not in Reinwardtia, which is closer by spelling).
  • For “Chrysophyllum madagascariensis”, Sapotaceae contain several species with this epithet, but only Gambeya madagascariensis belongs to an accepted species (Gambeya boiviniana) that also has a synonym in Chrysophyllum (Chrysophyllum boivinianum): Chrysophyllum species of Madagascar were moved to Gambeya.
  • “Palma colorada” is a local name. Palma Mill. is a synonym of Phoenix, so the genus fall-back is not used and the name stays unmatched.

Matches found by these steps are flagged and should be checked. Fuzzy matching cannot recognise every local name: names that are themselves in the backbone (such as the genus Guayaba) are matched, and agrep() can find a local name within a longer scientific name, giving a large Fuzzy.dist.

6. Explore 

WFO.synonyms("Gambeya boiviniana", WFO.data = WFO.example2026, verbose = FALSE)
#>           taxonID                      scientificName scientificNameAuthorship
#>            <char>                              <char>                   <char>
#> 1: wfo-0000970694                  Gambeya boiviniana                   Pierre
#> 2: wfo-0000854394           Chrysophyllum boivinianum          (Pierre) Baehni
#> 3: wfo-0000970695 Gambeya boiviniana var. lavanchiana                  Aubrév.
#> 4: wfo-0000970706            Gambeya madagascariensis                  Lecomte
#>    taxonRank taxonomicStatus acceptedNameUsageID
#>       <char>          <char>              <char>
#> 1:   species        Accepted                    
#> 2:   species         Synonym      wfo-0000970694
#> 3:   variety         Synonym      wfo-0000970694
#> 4:   species         Synonym      wfo-0000970694
fam <- WFO.family("Gambeya boiviniana",
  WFO.data = WFO.example2026, verbose = FALSE
)
fam[, c("Family", "Order", "Node.1")]
#>         Family    Order   Node.1
#> 333 Sapotaceae Ericales Eudicots
WFO.url(edge[1, ])
#> [1] "http://worldfloraonline.org/taxon/wfo-0000404362"

WFO.browse() lists the genera of a family, the species of a genus or the infraspecific taxa of a species.

7. Other backbones

Any taxonomic list with identifiers, names, authors and accepted-name identifiers can be used instead of the WFO:

mammals <- data.frame(
  id = c("M1", "M2"), name = c("Felis catus", "Felis domesticus"),
  author = c("Linnaeus, 1758", "Erxleben, 1777"), accepted = c("", "M1")
)
bb <- WFO.backbone(mammals,
  taxonID = "id", scientificName = "name",
  scientificNameAuthorship = "author", acceptedNameUsageID = "accepted"
)
m <- WFO.match("Felis domestica", WFO.data = bb, verbose = FALSE)
m[, c("spec.name", "scientificName", "Old.name")]
#>         spec.name scientificName         Old.name
#> 1 Felis domestica    Felis catus Felis domesticus

Performance

With the WFO Plant List 2026-06 (1.66 million names), matching 50,000 records takes about 5 seconds, and a misspelled name about 0.3 seconds:

  • the backbone is indexed once, so exact matches and accepted names are hash lookups;
  • each distinct name is fuzzy-matched once (in parallel with cores = n on Linux and macOS);
  • before each agrep() search, an exact prefilter discards names that cannot be within the allowed number of edits;
  • the index is kept for the next call with the same backbone, so that further calls take a fraction of a second. Keep the backbone as the data.table returned by WFO.read() or WFO.remember(): a data.frame is copied at each call.

With Fuzzy.keep.genus, Fuzzy.epithet.check and Fuzzy.skip.placeholder set to FALSE (the optional steps are off by default), results are those of WorldFlora 1.14-5 apart from the corrections listed in news(package = "WorldFloraFast").

Reference

Kindt, R. (2020). WorldFlora: An R package for exact and fuzzy matching of plant names against the World Flora Online taxonomic backbone data. Applications in Plant Sciences 8(9): e11388. https://doi.org/10.1002/aps3.11388
